channel.title: Middle East AI Monitor
channel.description: AI monitoring of Israel/Gaza, Iran, Syria, Lebanon and Iraq developments

item.title: Zach Bryan’s ‘Free Palestine’ shirt shows how political pressure can backfire on Israel - analysis
item.description: Most major musicians are not wearing “Free Palestine” shirts. However, if artists feel they are being pressured not to do so, it is possible that more of them will.

item.title: Israel's Transport Ministry denies role in vetting pilots as flydubai hijacking probe unfolds
item.description: Netanyahu assigned foreign-flight security to the ministry in 2025, but officials now say intelligence vetting of foreign pilots falls outside its remit.

item.title: Iran-backed militias trample US flag, exposing Iraq’s sovereignty problem - analysis
item.description: The trampling of the American flag by the militias is not new. However, the US will now focus on its activities after leaving Iraq. Iraq is talking about “sovereignty.”

item.title: No attempt to influence Israeli election, says Sinwar mediator who revealed Oct. 7 warning
item.description: Referring to the attack Hamas launched on Israel three years ago on October 7, Abu Zaida described it as "a reckless gamble based on mistaken calculations and assessments."

item.title: Irish soccer team's coach cuts press conference short after heated exchange with Israeli journalist
item.description: An Israeli journalist asked why Irish players allegedly called Israeli players “monkeys” during their previous match, prompting the coach to leave the press conference.

item.title: Emily Damari shares unreleased hostage photos, says surviving Hamas captivity was a miracle
item.description: "Three years ago at this time on Simchat Torah I was deep, deep in the Gaza Strip," Damari wrote in her post.

item.title: Israel to close West Bank, Gaza crossings for October 7 remembrance ceremonies, COGAT says
item.description: During the closure, passage through crossings in the West Bank will be permitted only in humanitarian, medical, and other exceptional cases, subject to COGAT approval.

item.title: The dream of normalization with Saudi Arabia clouded Netanyahu’s judgment - opinion
item.description: Three years after October 7, it is becoming increasingly clear that the question of normalization with Saudi Arabia lay at the heart of the calculations and thinking on both sides.

item.title: IDF to equip combat engineering vehicles with Iron Fist active protection against anti-tank threats
item.description: Iron Fist, manufactured by Elbit Systems, is an active protection system designed to protect armored fighting vehicles and engineering vehicles.

item.title: Awake Jerusalem to bring Christian leaders from 51 nations to Tower of David
item.description: The October 3 music festival is part of a ten-day Eagles’ Wings delegation that has brought more than 550 Christian leaders to Israel ahead of the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks

item.title: No. 1: Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump: Remembering who brought the hostages home
item.description: Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump helped achieve what few in Jerusalem thought possible, bringing every Israeli hostage home and reshaping the Middle East.

item.title: No. 3: Gadi Eisenkot: Israel’s next prime minister?
item.description: The former IDF chief has emerged as the leading opposition challenger to Netanyahu, offering voters a path to a post-Netanyahu Israel.

item.title: No. 4: Naftali Bennett: The former PM seeking a comeback to ‘repair Israel’
item.description: Since returning to politics, Bennett has shifted from his previous campaigns, taking a more liberal position while maintaining a strong right-wing stance on security.

item.title: No. 5: Ronald Lauder: Standing at the forefront of the fight against antisemitism
item.description: Lauder has never confined himself to quiet philanthropy - he continues to use his position to demand accountability from political leaders.

item.title: No. 2: Benjamin Netanyahu: Shaping Israel’s politics and global image for a generation
item.description: Netanyahu has become more than Israel’s prime minister for many. Abroad, for instance, he has become Israel’s symbol and the lightning rod for much of the hatred directed against the Jewish state.

item.title: As elections loom, voters must choose the right pilot to navigate political turbulence - editorial
item.description: The passengers aboard the flydubai flight did not have the luxury of leaving the cockpit unresolved. Israeli voters will have their own chance to take control and choose who sits in the cockpit.

item.title: Halevi: Netanyahu rejected firing reservists who stopped reporting amid judicial reform - report
item.description: According to N12, after the Knesset approved the law eliminating the reasonableness standard, Halevi met with the prime minister and warned him that Israel was entering a dangerous situation.

item.title: Defense Ministry: 1,318 Israeli security personnel killed across all fronts since October 7
item.description: The number includes fallen personnel from the IDF, Israel Police, Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency), Fire and Rescue Services, security coordinators, and local response team members.

item.title: Woman arrested in northern Israel over alleged false terror report, husband arrested over threats
item.description: Police said extensive checks ruled out any security-related intent on the husband’s part and raised a “clear suspicion” that the woman’s warning about an impending attack was entirely false.

item.title: Netanyahu: 'Britain still an ally of Israel,' even if gov't 'appeases our enemies, attacks us'
item.description: "When they appease our common enemies and attack us, it doesn't say much," Netanyahu said about the current relationship with the UK government during an interview with The Daily Mail.
